title: A 2,000-Year-Old Gold Ring in Thailand Had an Indian Inscription
mediaSource: ancient gold ring Brahmi inscription Thailand burial archaeology trade network India Southeast Asia

scenes.title: An Indian inscription was found in a Thai grave
scenes.narration: A gold ring found in a roughly 2,000-year-old grave in Thailand carried a surprise. Its inscription was written not in a local script, but in ancient Indian Brahmi.

scenes.title: It came from the Don Yai Thong site
scenes.narration: The ring was uncovered at a burial site called Don Yai Thong in Thailand's Phetchaburi Province. Other ornaments and traces of long-distance exchange were found in the area as well.

scenes.title: The inscription may identify its owner
scenes.narration: The Brahmi inscription reads pusarakhitasa, interpreted as meaning a person protected by Pushya. It may have functioned like a personal name or identifying phrase.
keywords: ancient Indian writing inscription close up

scenes.title: Ancient Thailand was already connected internationally
scenes.narration: Researchers say the find supports evidence that communities in this part of Thailand were linked to trade networks stretching between India and Vietnam around 2,000 years ago.
keywords: ancient trade route India Southeast Asia map

scenes.title: Its owner may have been connected to trade
scenes.narration: Experts have suggested that the ring's owner may have belonged to a merchant-related social group. That would fit with the broader evidence for active long-distance exchange in the region.
keywords: ancient merchant India Southeast Asia artifact

scenes.title: One tiny ring reveals an ancient network
scenes.narration: Modern borders make these places feel far apart, but people, goods, and ideas were already moving across South and Southeast Asia two millennia ago. One small ring preserves that connection.
